papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving—sometimes even improving—task performance. Methods operate at the level of logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision boundaries and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and federated or data-free workflows. Practical deployments require careful alignment of teacher and student inputs and objectives, attention to data availability and privacy, and strategies for dealing with capacity gaps and distributional heterogeneity. Across vision, language, speech, recommender, and multimodal tasks, tailored distillation pipelines enable compact models suitable for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from simple teacher-to-student logit matching into a broad toolkit for compressing, adapting, and deploying deep models across vision, language, multimodal, and structured domains. Modern KD transfers soft targets, intermediate representations, relational and contrastive structures, or synthesized data; it operates in offline, online, multi-teacher, cross-modal, and data-constrained regimes and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while reducing compute, memory, and latency, but success depends on teacher quality, capacity matching, data/augmentation strategy, and careful design of objectives and layer mappings. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, applications, and practical recommendations documented in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their capabilities. KD enables deployment across modalities and constrained environments, and empirical work shows it can approach teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques. However, KD is not a universal solution: it can propagate teacher errors and biases, struggle under data scarcity or mismatch, and require careful choices of distilled targets, architectures, and training schedules. To realize KD's benefits in production and research settings, practitioners should pair distillation with targeted remedies—representation-aware objectives, data-and-curriculum strategies, ensemble or adversarial schemes, and fairness or privacy interventions—tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies have become central to deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, multimodal, and language domains, researchers have developed approaches that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students via logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or adversarial objectives. Work spans supervised and unsupervised settings, data-free or black-box scenarios, continual and federated use-cases, and concerns such as privacy and adversarial robustness. Practical recipes combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, progressive module replacement, and many-to-many layer mapping to balance accuracy, latency, and memory. Open challenges remain in data- and domain-limited regimes, robust and private compression, and principled selection of which teacher knowledge to transfer for a given downstream task.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compressing large models for deployment and domain-specific use. Across modalities and tasks, KD can preserve much of the teacher's performance in compact students, but it must be combined with task-aware engineering—such as teacher adaptation, layer-wise selection, data augmentation, and hardware-aware pruning—to address heterogeneity, domain shift, and efficiency constraints. This article argues that KD is necessary but not sufficient: best results come from integrating KD with complementary techniques chosen for the target modality, deployment constraints, and learning scenario.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more specialized ones. This synthesis summarizes methods for transferring output-level and internal representations, architectural and layer-wise strategies for compression, training variants (e.g., self-supervised, adversarial, few-shot, online, and federated settings), and applications across NLP, vision, generative models, graph learning, and distributed systems. It highlights empirical findings on when distillation is most effective, techniques to preserve or improve robustness and fairness, and practical strategies for heterogeneous and latency-sensitive deployments. Gaps and recurring challenges are identified to guide future work.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or adapts large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, generative models, and domain- or privacy-constrained settings, a diverse toolbox has been developed—soft-label supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and architecture-aware adaptations (e.g., pruning, layer skipping, NAS). Empirical results show that appropriately designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments, while practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and optimization design. Remaining challenges include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures or non-iid data, privacy-and-fairness-aware protocols, and extending KD to complex generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD methods vary by what is transferred (teacher logits, internal representations, attention, relational structure), how layers are aligned or projected, and how data constraints (limited access, privacy, or distribution shift) are handled. Empirical work demonstrates that combining output-level and representation-level objectives, using layer-mapping or projector modules, and adapting training data or curricula yields the best trade-offs between compactness and accuracy. Despite wide success, effective distillation requires careful choices about teacher quality, distilled signals, sample selection, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Pragmatic, Task-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings, distillation can preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployments with constrained compute, memory, latency, and privacy requirements. However, its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints (e.g., robustness, heterogeneity, data availability). When applied thoughtfully—using feature-based objectives, ensemble or adversarial strategies, data augmentation or data-free approaches, and task-adaptive compression—KD reliably delivers practical trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Yet Contextual, Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has repeatedly enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost across modalities while retaining much of the performance of larger models. Empirical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, inductive biases, and task-specific capabilities from teacher to student, and can be adapted via logit-, feature-, and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, adversarial procedures, and data- or privacy-aware variants. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization difficulties, teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity, and propagation of teacher errors limit its effectiveness unless combined with careful protocol design and complementary compression techniques. I argue KD should be treated as a first-class tool in compression toolkits, but only when used with task-aware filtering, capacity-aware targets, and architecture- or data-aware refinements to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, structured prediction, and language tasks—KD variants (logit transfer, feature- and attention-matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols) provide concrete trade-offs between model size, compute, and accuracy. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, pruning, low-precision numerics, or privacy mechanisms, distillation enables robust deployment on resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive platforms. However, distillation outcomes depend on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and design choices for objectives and training pipelines; tailored practices are therefore needed to realize KD's full potential and avoid failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression strategies form a broad, practically driven toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, graph learning, self-supervision, and reinforcement learning—research has developed many algorithmic variants (logit and feature matching, attention/relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes), system-level protocols (federated, black-box, data-free), and architecture-aware methods (task-adaptive compression, neural architecture search, pruning and quantization combinations). Empirically, KD often substantially reduces latency and parameter counts while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher–student alignment, available data and augmentations, and task-specific design; remaining challenges include teacher bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and heterogeneous-device constraints. Practical deployments balance distilled signals, data strategies, and architecture choices to achieve required trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable technique for compressing and adapting large neural models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across computer vision, generative modeling, cross-modal systems, and NLP, distillation can be combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, adversarial training, and feature alignment) to meet deployment constraints and domain requirements. Success depends on teacher design, the availability and nature of data used for transfer, careful alignment of representations, and training objectives that address optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Necessity, Limitations, and a Consolidated Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high‑performing deep models in resource‑constrained settings across vision, speech, recommendation, graph, and language tasks. KD delivers large efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: teacher inference cost, data mismatches introduced by distillation, low‑frequency token degradation, privacy considerations, and heterogeneous deployment constraints each demand tailored remedies. Combining complementary strategies — multi‑teacher distillation, student‑aware teacher design, projector/feature adaptation, self‑distillation, exposure to raw data, and privacy-aware or federated KD — yields robust compressed models that approach or match teacher capabilities in practice.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Path for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from teacher models. Across tasks and modalities, distillation methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and structure-preserving objectives—enable deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory use, and communication cost. Distillation also serves as a flexible substrate for addressing domain adaptation, lifelong learning, robustness, low-precision deployment, and generator compression. However, realizing these benefits in practice requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to map layers and representations, how to handle limited or private teacher data, and how to mitigate bias or robustness loss.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Compression and Robust Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential technique for compressing large models and transferring useful knowledge to smaller or specialized models. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, distillation enables faster inference, reduced memory footprint, and sometimes improved generalization when combined with complementary strategies (e.g., architecture search, pruning, or data management). However, distillation outcomes depend on data, teacher-student alignment, and training design; success requires adapting KD objectives and pipelines to the task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When adapted to task, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of a teacher's performance while enabling lower latency, smaller memory footprint, and improved adaptability across domains and modalities. However, KD is a family of techniques rather than a single algorithm: best outcomes arise from combining distillation with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, architecture search, curriculum design, data synthesis) and from explicitly addressing challenges such as imperfect teachers, domain shift, privacy, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Integrated Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the functionality of larger teachers. KD works across modalities, supports deployment under resource and privacy constraints, and also acts as a regularizer; however, it has concrete failure modes that require complementary methods and careful teacher–student design. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of any compression pipeline, used in combination with representation-aware objectives, curriculum and data strategies, and targeted safeguards for bias, low-frequency behavior, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained student models so they retain functionality while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logits-based soft-label supervision to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware mappings, adversarial and contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or heterogeneous-device protocols. Empirical and theoretical work indicates KD often acts both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, task alignment, and careful design of objectives and model interfaces. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data scarcity or domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, principled layer-to-layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating teacher-induced biases.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Modalities, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high-performing deep learning models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. A broad set of distillation strategies—ranging from soft-label supervision and feature mimicking to data-free (zero-shot) distillation, adversarially guided feature transfer, self-distillation, and automated architecture search guided by teacher models—enable substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while preserving or even improving performance across vision, language, multimodal, and sequence tasks. Best practice combines input-side methods (data augmentation and mixup), representation-level transfer, and careful teacher-student design choices to match the deployment objectives (efficiency, fairness, interpretability, or privacy).

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become primary approaches for deploying high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. The literature spans methods that transfer soft-labels, internal feature representations, and ensemble knowledge; extensions address teacher imperfections, data scarcity or privacy, task-specific adaptations for NLP and vision, and hardware-aware compression. Empirical work demonstrates that careful design choices—such as which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student layers, whether to incorporate self-distillation or multi-teacher training, and how to combine pruning or low-precision numerics—substantially affect final accuracy and efficiency. The field also benefits from theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Remaining challenges include distilling robust semantics for low-frequency phenomena, distillation without access to original data, and co-design for hardware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal domains, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance; it is most effective when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation, and hardware-aware design). The literature also highlights several persistent challenges — teacher and capacity mismatch, optimization and data limitations, privacy and distribution shift — and converges on practical strategies such as careful choice of distillation signals, layer alignment, multi-teacher or online protocols, and synthetic-data or data-free approaches to operate under constrained access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger or differently structured models to smaller or more efficient ones, reducing computational cost and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings. Approaches vary in what is transferred (logits/soft labels, intermediate representations, feature maps, attention or decision-boundary information), how the transfer is staged (offline teacher-student, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, ensemble distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving setups), and how training data or augmentation is used. Empirical results across computer vision, speech/lipreading, retrieval, translation, reading comprehension, CTR prediction, federated learning, GANs, NAS, and Transformer compression show that appropriate combination of distillation objective, data strategy, and model design can yield large gains in efficiency with modest or no loss in accuracy. Practical factors that shape success include teacher strength and mismatch to the student, the complexity of distilled data, the role of pre-training for compact models, targeted selection or augmentation of distillation samples, and orthogonal compression techniques such as structured pruning.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Non-Automatic Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows that KD can yield substantial reductions in parameter count and latency with modest accuracy loss, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Rather than a single recipe, KD is best treated as a principled toolbox: combine output-level and representation-level objectives, design student-aware teachers or progressive module replacement, and integrate KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and privacy/robustness safeguards to meet practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Demand-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' utility. KD methods span output matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, self- and ensemble-distillation, meta-learned and student-friendly teacher designs, and data- or task-aware adaptations. Empirical work across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks demonstrates KD’s ability to deliver large reductions in model size and compute with modest performance loss, and in many cases to improve robustness or generalization when combined with appropriate procedures. At the same time, KD’s reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these constraints through architectural design, curriculum and meta-learning, augmentation and synthetic-data strategies, and multi-teacher or online schemes is central to practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are now core tools for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. The literature has expanded far beyond simple logits matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, and tight integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates broad applicability across modalities (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and generative models) and deployment contexts (edge devices, federated systems, and data-constrained settings). The main practical challenges are (1) choosing what and how to distill for a given task and student architecture, (2) coping with limited or unavailable original training data, (3) avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses (e.g., biases or low-frequency degradation), and (4) co-designing distillation with other compression primitives and hardware constraints. Progress comes from combining representational objectives, layer-mapping strategies, task-aware teacher selection, and safeguards (privacy or fairness) appropriate to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained student models so they retain functionality while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logits-based soft-label supervision to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware mappings, adversarial and contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or heterogeneous-device protocols. Empirical and theoretical work indicates KD often acts both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, task alignment, and careful design of objectives and model interfaces. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data scarcity or domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, principled layer-to-layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating teacher-induced biases.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Practical, but Not Sufficiently Complete Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. KD techniques extend beyond logit matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, attention and projection-based mappings, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-constrained regimes (few-shot, data-free). KD reliably improves deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, and sometimes robustness or privacy), but it has concrete limits—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and task-specific design needs—that make KD most effective when integrated with complementary compression and training practices.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for transferring predictive behavior from large, expensive teachers to smaller, efficient students. Across vision, language, recommendation, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD has been extended beyond logits-matching into feature and layer-level mimicry, online and self-distillation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, task-adaptive architecture search, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical results show KD enables substantial latency and memory reductions while often preserving accuracy, improving calibration, and helping robustness; success depends strongly on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, data and augmentation, and alignment strategies between heterogeneous models.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable technique for compressing and adapting large neural models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across computer vision, generative modeling, cross-modal systems, and NLP, distillation can be combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, adversarial training, and feature alignment) to meet deployment constraints and domain requirements. Success depends on teacher design, the availability and nature of data used for transfer, careful alignment of representations, and training objectives that address optimization challenges.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis reviews empirical and methodological advances in knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques as applied across vision, language, generative models, retrieval, recommender systems, federated and lifelong learning. It summarizes mechanisms for transferring teacher knowledge to smaller students (soft labels, intermediate representations, curriculum and selective sample strategies), practical challenges (data availability, teacher cost, domain shift, privacy, and bias), and targeted solutions (data-free distillation, fast label generation, multi-teacher and domain-adaptive schemes, self-distillation, and distillation-aware pruning). The goal is to map what the provided literature reports about when distillation helps, when it can hurt, and which strategies are effective for different settings and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical, and theoretically grounded approach to compressing and adapting deep models. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables compact students to inherit predictive performance, inductive biases, and application-specific properties (privacy, fairness, task-adaptivity) from larger or specialized teachers. Best practice combines logit-level, feature-level, and architecture-aware strategies, often augmented by multi-teacher, curriculum, or meta-learning schemes; privacy-preserving and data-free variants make KD suitable for sensitive or decentralized settings. We argue that KD should be a first-class tool in compression toolkits and outline concrete practices that are supported by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more specialized ones. This synthesis summarizes methods for transferring output-level and internal representations, architectural and layer-wise strategies for compression, training variants (e.g., self-supervised, adversarial, few-shot, online, and federated settings), and applications across NLP, vision, generative models, graph learning, and distributed systems. It highlights empirical findings on when distillation is most effective, techniques to preserve or improve robustness and fairness, and practical strategies for heterogeneous and latency-sensitive deployments. Gaps and recurring challenges are identified to guide future work.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, structured prediction, and language tasks—KD variants (logit transfer, feature- and attention-matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols) provide concrete trade-offs between model size, compute, and accuracy. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, pruning, low-precision numerics, or privacy mechanisms, distillation enables robust deployment on resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive platforms. However, distillation outcomes depend on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and design choices for objectives and training pipelines; tailored practices are therefore needed to realize KD's full potential and avoid failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. The literature shows a diverse set of objectives and protocols—soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, many-to-many layer mappings, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and adversarial or generator-based sample augmentation—that together enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while trading off accuracy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical results indicate distilled students often approach teacher performance with substantially lower cost, but important limitations persist (teacher bias transfer, low-frequency token degradation, data access constraints, and capacity mismatch), motivating hybrid pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful teacher–student design.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central strategies for deploying large deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of methods—ranging from soft-label distillation, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer mapping, adversarial and data-free techniques, to task-adaptive architecture search and meta-learning of teachers—have been proposed to transfer performance from bulky teachers to compact students. These approaches are applied across domains including vision, language, multi-modal systems, recommender systems, and domain-specific NLP, and they trade off fidelity to the teacher, generalization, and computational efficiency. Empirical results show that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while yielding substantial speedups and memory reductions, and in some settings can even improve fairness, robustness, or downstream generalization. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and representations across teacher and student, coping with absent or private training data, and automatically selecting what and how to transfer for specific tasks and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger systems. Across modalities and tasks—including classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and sequence prediction—distillation has been adapted to transfer ensemble knowledge, reduce computation and storage, improve generalization and fairness, enable private or federated deployment, and inject specialized inductive biases. While effective, distillation requires careful design choices (teacher quality, which examples to transfer, whether to use intermediate-layer alignment, robustness and privacy mechanisms) to avoid failure modes. This work argues that KD should be treated not just as a compression trick but as a unifying framework for controlled transfer of behaviors, and outlines empirical and theoretical findings that guide best practices for its application.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a broadly useful means to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller students so that compressed models can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when it is adapted to the problem: what to transfer (logits, features, attention), which data to use or synthesize, how to weight multiple teachers or imperfect supervision, and how to integrate complementary compression techniques. However, KD is neither automatic nor sufficient on its own: careful, task-aware design and combination with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies are required to realize reliable, production-ready compression.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques for compressing large or expensive models into smaller, faster, or more deployable ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Methods differ in the form of transferred knowledge (soft logits, hidden features, contrastive distributions, synthetic data, or cross-modal alignments), in how and when distillation is applied (offline, online, layer-wise, task-adaptive, or data-free), and in the problems they target (classification, detection, generation, language tasks, graph learning, or novel-view synthesis). Empirical work demonstrates that appropriate choices about teacher signals, data manipulation, and architectural search can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities; theoretical work begins to clarify when soft labels help and when hard labels or mixed supervision are needed. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, dataset and fairness concerns, and scaling distillation reliably in large distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners transfer logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision-boundary information and combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover most teacher performance and, in some cases, match or exceed teachers when distillation is paired with careful teacher design, layer mapping, and data or training schedules. Major limitations remain in imperfect belief matching, distribution shift, handling low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data, and principled teacher selection—areas where methodological and theoretical progress continues to be needed.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad toolbox for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models to smaller, faster, or privacy-preserving models. Methods range from soft-logit supervision to internal representation matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence across vision, NLP, graphs, and federated settings shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance in resource-constrained deployments, while challenges remain in teacher selection, data availability, bias propagation, and task-specific design.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression comprise a diverse set of techniques to produce smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger or auxiliary models. Research spans supervised teacher-student frameworks, self-distillation, multi-teacher and task-adaptive compression, and distillation combined with pruning, architecture search, adversarial training, and data augmentation. Practical work demonstrates benefits across vision, multimodal, graph, and NLP tasks, while theoretical analyses connect distillation to label smoothing, ensemble behavior, and bias–variance tradeoffs. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and modalities, preserving robustness and privacy, and handling low-resource or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used to compress large neural models for deployment under resource constraints and to transfer task- and domain-specific priors across models. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal problems, distillation methods go beyond matching output probabilities: modern approaches match intermediate representations, attention patterns, contrastive structure, and task-specific signals. Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs and architectures, choosing losses that capture relational or localized information, addressing dataset shifts (including low-frequency token behavior), and carefully choosing which teacher signals to transfer. Several family-specific solutions (detection, retrieval, non-autoregressive translation, graph learning, vision-language, and spoken QA) show distillation can both improve accuracy and reduce inference cost, but raise challenges around data availability, heterogeneity, and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. KD has been shown to work across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It can also be combined with data augmentation, adversarial schemes, online or teacher-free training, and architecture-aware adaptations to meet deployment constraints. KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about which teacher signals to transfer, alignment of inputs and architectures, student capacity, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. When used as part of a task-aware compression pipeline that addresses these issues, KD delivers substantial practical benefits for latency- and resource-constrained deployments.

Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods.
