papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative modeling, researchers transfer information via softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, relational and attention maps, and many-to-many layer alignment. Variants address resource heterogeneity, data unavailability, privacy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical and analytic work shows that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, but its success depends on design choices (what to transfer, teacher quality, data or pseudo-data, and alignment losses). State-of-the-art practice mixes logits-based loss with feature- or representation-level objectives, task-aware augmentations, and architecture- or training-aware modifications to obtain favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis reviews empirical and methodological advances in knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques as applied across vision, language, generative models, retrieval, recommender systems, federated and lifelong learning. It summarizes mechanisms for transferring teacher knowledge to smaller students (soft labels, intermediate representations, curriculum and selective sample strategies), practical challenges (data availability, teacher cost, domain shift, privacy, and bias), and targeted solutions (data-free distillation, fast label generation, multi-teacher and domain-adaptive schemes, self-distillation, and distillation-aware pruning). The goal is to map what the provided literature reports about when distillation helps, when it can hurt, and which strategies are effective for different settings and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are widely used to transfer behavior from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Work across vision, generative modeling, reinforcement learning, recommendation, and language has developed diverse objectives and mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, adversarial synthesis of training data, multi-teacher/ensemble supervision, layer-wise and task-adaptive compression, and data-augmentation-enhanced distillation. These approaches trade off accuracy, inference cost, and robustness and address practical constraints such as lack of access to original training data, domain shift, fairness, and heterogeneous model architectures. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or sometimes match teacher performance while substantially reducing FLOPs, parameters, or latency, but limitations remain in data heterogeneity, low-frequency token transfer, and privacy-constrained settings. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical findings, applications, and open challenges documented in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers across vision, language, graph, and generative settings. KD supports deployment on constrained hardware, domain adaptation, improved interpretability, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, data and augmentation choices, objective design, and handling of distributional or architectural mismatch. Careful engineering and complementary compression techniques are necessary to realize KD's benefits in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile framework that enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component—combining logits, intermediate-feature matching, contrastive objectives, data augmentation, and privacy-aware techniques—distillation supports deployment across modalities and constrained devices. However, KD is not automatic: it propagates some teacher errors, can lose low-frequency or structured information, and requires careful design choices (teacher selection, objective weighting, data strategy). A principled practice that matches the distillation objective to the task, augments or tailors distillation data, and applies privacy- or domain-aware protocols yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger or specialized models. Approaches span from simple soft-label supervision to richer transfers of internal representations, intermediate-layer mappings, attention-guided projections, adversarial feature alignment, and task- or device-aware compression. KD is used across domains—image classification, detection (2D and 3D), recommendation/CTR, language model compression, federated and heterogeneous-device learning, and reinforcement learning—and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or curriculum strategies. Recent work examines theoretical aspects (e.g., bias–variance tradeoffs and statistical interactions with data augmentation), practical design choices (teacher-student layer alignment, many-to-many mappings, ensemble teachers), and extensions that address privacy, fairness, and low-data regimes. Despite strong empirical success, open problems remain in understanding when particular KD variants best transfer generalization, how to measure and mitigate transferred biases, and how to optimally combine KD with other compression primitives for different constraints.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach to compress large or ensemble models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, distillation can recover accuracy for lightweight architectures, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and transfer specialized properties (e.g., temporal, structural, or ensemble knowledge). However, distillation is not a panacea: its success depends on the choice of teacher, student architecture and capacity, the training protocol (including data augmentation and sample selection), and implementation details that affect optimization. When these factors are treated carefully, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, architecture design, quantization) and can be adapted to domain-specific needs such as federated learning, retrieval, and vision-language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool That Requires Context-Aware Integration
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, widely applicable technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models to compact students across vision, language, generative, and distributed settings. However, KD is not a silver bullet; its success depends on teacher quality, choice of distilled signals, available data, and optimization procedures. For practical, high-fidelity compression, KD should be treated as a core component of a broader pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, careful layer- and feature-level alignment, multi-teacher or meta-learned teaching strategies, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods such as pruning or quantization.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide a practical path to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Across vision and language, researchers have explored teacher-student training, intermediate-layer alignment, data- and label-space manipulations, data-free or few-shot settings, and architecture-aware compression. These techniques can preserve much of a teacher's performance while yielding smaller, faster models, and they can be combined with pruning, architecture search, or ensemble compression. KD also intersects with concerns about fairness, generalization, and privacy, and its effectiveness depends on design choices such as the form of distilled targets, data augmentation, and the match between teacher, student, and task.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compressing large models for deployment and domain-specific use. Across modalities and tasks, KD can preserve much of the teacher's performance in compact students, but it must be combined with task-aware engineering—such as teacher adaptation, layer-wise selection, data augmentation, and hardware-aware pruning—to address heterogeneity, domain shift, and efficiency constraints. This article argues that KD is necessary but not sufficient: best results come from integrating KD with complementary techniques chosen for the target modality, deployment constraints, and learning scenario.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from large, often multi-modal or ensemble teachers into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD has been adapted into many forms — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and offline protocols, and data-free or zero-shot schemes — and is frequently combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance in many settings when teacher quality, student capacity, and appropriate data or synthesis strategies are addressed; theoretical and empirical analyses highlight KD’s role both as knowledge transfer and as a regularizer. Despite broad success, KD faces limits from teacher–student mismatch, limited or heterogeneous data, and propagation of teacher artifacts; current best practice is to treat KD as one element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for compressing neural networks into a broad, practically validated family of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the functionality of larger teachers. KD methods transfer information via outputs, intermediate features, relational signals, or synthesized data, and they are applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, multimodal) and problem classes (classification, detection, generation, reinforcement learning, segmentation, view synthesis). Practical success depends on matching the distillation strategy to the task and deployment constraints (data availability, privacy, capacity, latency, hardware), and on integrating KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware adaptations. Remaining challenges include teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviour in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have matured into a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or more private models. Across computer vision, NLP, multimodal systems, federated settings, and generative models, researchers have combined soft-label (logit) distillation, intermediate feature/hint transfer, architecture transformation, quantization, pruning, and automated search to achieve significant reductions in memory, computation, or communication while largely preserving accuracy. Empirical work demonstrates that distillation can enable high-quality low-precision models, speed up inference and training, unify heterogeneous models without shared data, and make distributed learning more communication- and privacy-efficient. The field continues to refine when and what knowledge to transfer (e.g., logits vs. features vs. attention), how to handle multiple or unreliable teachers, how to design student-friendly teachers, and how to integrate distillation with other compression methods such as pruning and search.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: The Case for Task- and Data-Aware Knowledge Distillation: Principles, Pitfalls, and Practical Extensions for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical success across vision, language, graph, and generative models depends not only on the generic teacher→student paradigm but on task-aware selection of transferred information, choices about data access (including data-free and privacy-preserving variants), and the use of auxiliary techniques (adversarial training, ensembling, pruning, and architecture search). When these dimensions are addressed explicitly, distillation can produce compact models that approach teacher performance while offering improved robustness, interpretability, or resource-efficiency. However, naive distillation can fail due to optimization difficulties, domain shift, and heterogeneous teacher-student mismatches, so practitioners must adopt targeted strategies that consider the learning objective, available data, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable strategy for compressing deep models across modalities and tasks. It can preserve much of a teacher's performance while reducing memory, computation, and inference latency; it also enables task-adaptive and privacy-conscious deployments. Remaining challenges—data availability, matching student capacity to teacher signals, and choosing the right transfer targets—can be mitigated by a suite of complementary KD techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, generative modeling, and federated settings. A broad set of techniques—matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, adversarial and curriculum-based sample selection, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, and data- or privacy-aware generation—enable students to retain much of teacher performance while reducing parameters, latency, and memory. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but limitations persist (teacher errors, optimization gaps, domain and data mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, and heterogeneity of devices/architectures). Advances such as feature-based distillation, curriculum strategies, adversarial sample use, many-to-many layer alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and teacher-free/self-distillation extend applicability and mitigate failure modes. Key open problems include principled theory for which teacher signals matter across tasks, robust private and data-free distillation, and automated co-design of student architectures and distillation objectives for heterogeneous deployments.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, and multimodal settings. It can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, and it interacts naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, distillation's success depends on the distillation objective, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and task-specific considerations; when these are not addressed it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with rare outputs, or fail due to optimization issues. Best practice is to treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits, intermediate feature matching, projector modules, multi-teacher or teacher-adaptive designs, and data-aware schedules—to maximize student utility in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained student models so they retain functionality while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Over the past decade KD has evolved from logits-based soft-label supervision to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware mappings, adversarial and contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and federated or heterogeneous-device protocols. Empirical and theoretical work indicates KD often acts both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, task alignment, and careful design of objectives and model interfaces. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data scarcity or domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, principled layer-to-layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating teacher-induced biases.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression trick into a broad set of techniques that enable efficient deployment, cross-modal transfer, federated and privacy-preserving learning, and improved generalization across domains. Empirical results across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs) show that KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while retaining most of the teacher performance. However, the success of KD depends on careful choices — teacher quality, what to distill (outputs, features, internal representations), data availability and augmentation, and the loss or alignment mechanism — and recent work proposes multiple refinements (multi-teacher schemes, adversarial critics, projector modules, teacher-free variants) that mitigate known failure modes. The balance of empirical evidence and theoretical analyses indicates that KD is both practically indispensable for many compression tasks and a fertile area for research on how knowledge should be measured, transferred, and regularized.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Necessity, Limits, and a Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling reduced memory, lower-latency inference, and new capabilities such as task-adaptive compression, multi-task transfer, and interpretable surrogates. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, dataset and distribution mismatches, teacher bias transfer, and design choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational structure) strongly affect outcomes. The most reliable results come from combining KD with complementary techniques (teacher adaptation, selective or curriculum-driven sample selection, representation matching, low-precision numerics, and scaled training procedures) and from tailoring the procedure to task- and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or specialized teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed many variants—logit transfer, feature- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives, ensemble- and teacher-aware algorithms, data-free and few-shot protocols, and meta-learned teachers—to address practical deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, device heterogeneity) while also pursuing robustness, fairness, and task adaptation. This synthesis summarizes dominant methods, representative applications, empirical patterns, and common failure modes that guide practical use and future research.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Practical, but Not Sufficiently Complete Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. KD techniques extend beyond logit matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, attention and projection-based mappings, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-constrained regimes (few-shot, data-free). KD reliably improves deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, and sometimes robustness or privacy), but it has concrete limits—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and task-specific design needs—that make KD most effective when integrated with complementary compression and training practices.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression and Responsible Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a versatile, task- and domain-adaptive toolbox rather than a single recipe. When combined with complementary mechanisms (feature and layer matching, many-to-many alignment, data augmentation, ensembling, pruning, quantization, and privacy-preserving protocols), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving—or in some cases improving—task performance. Realizing these benefits reliably requires attention to what is distilled, how teacher and student are matched, and measures to mitigate risks such as teacher bias, data scarcity, and privacy concerns. Practical adoption should therefore treat KD as a configurable component of compression and deployment pipelines, with choices driven by the task, data availability, and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Context-Dependent Tools for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression provide a practical, widely applicable route to produce smaller, faster, and often more robust models from larger teachers across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. When combined with representation-matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on teacher quality, the data used for distillation, careful choice of what is transferred, and attention to fairness and domain-shift risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an essential yet context-sensitive component of model deployment pipelines, and summarizes best-practice recommendations and promising directions to make distillation reliably effective in applied settings.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more deployable models by transferring information from larger or specialized models. It supports a broad range of objectives beyond raw compression—improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, supporting privacy-aware or federated workflows, and permitting deployment on constrained hardware. KD methods range from simple soft-label matching to richer transfers of intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational or contrastive structure. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, alignment between teacher and student, data availability and distribution, and the choice of signals and losses. When applied with attention to these constraints and combined sensibly with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), KD is a practical foundational technique for real-world model compression in vision, language, and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a primary practical technique for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD supports a wide variety of goals—reducing latency and memory, enabling on-device inference, preserving privacy when data are unavailable, and transferring robustness or domain knowledge—by varying what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational/contrastive signals) and how training is scheduled (offline, online, progressive replacement, or data-free synthesis). While KD is not a universal cure, its flexibility and empirical success make it a first-choice strategy for compression when combined with careful design choices about teacher quality, transfer signals, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but computationally expensive neural networks in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more specialized ones. This synthesis summarizes methods for transferring output-level and internal representations, architectural and layer-wise strategies for compression, training variants (e.g., self-supervised, adversarial, few-shot, online, and federated settings), and applications across NLP, vision, generative models, graph learning, and distributed systems. It highlights empirical findings on when distillation is most effective, techniques to preserve or improve robustness and fairness, and practical strategies for heterogeneous and latency-sensitive deployments. Gaps and recurring challenges are identified to guide future work.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have evolved from a simple teacher-to-student logits-matching recipe into a broad toolbox for producing compact, efficient, and adaptable models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Research has produced a range of practical methods—logit and feature matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data- and privacy-aware variants, and federated or online protocols—and has clarified connections to regularization, ensemble learning, and optimization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher's performance, though gains depend on teacher quality, data used for distillation, and adaptation to deployment constraints. This synthesis summarizes core methods, theoretical insights, empirical findings, practical considerations, and open challenges that shape current best practice for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central for deploying large deep models in latency- and resource-constrained settings. Across modalities and tasks, a consistent pattern is that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation addresses mismatches in architecture, data distribution, and input representations. Practical advances include multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, online and distributed distillation, data-free and zero-shot approaches, layer-wise and many-to-many layer mappings, task-aware selection of distilled information, and distillation formulations tailored to domain adaptation and federated settings. Theoretical and empirical analyses point to KD acting both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; performance depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data augmentation, and instance-level selection of teacher signals. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, principled teacher selection, and aligning intermediate representations across heterogeneous detectors or modalities.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Limitations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible method for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models across vision, language, speech, and recommendation systems. KD works both as a stand-alone compression technique and as a complementary tool that combines well with pruning, quantization, multi-teacher strategies, and privacy-aware or federated settings. While highly effective in practice, KD has limits—especially around data availability, heterogeneity, and theoretical understanding—that recent work addresses with data-free methods, meta-learning teachers, and principled analyses.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational, Versatile, but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment, privacy, and latency constraints. KD spans logits-based supervision, representation and feature matching, adversarial and generator-based data synthesis, multi-teacher or online schemes, and task- and domain-aware adaptations. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful training practices (projectors, curriculum, selective sampling), KD can recover much of teacher performance and enable new capabilities (cross-domain transfer, federated heterogeneity, and multi-modal compression). However, KD is not a turnkey solution: success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or few-shot regimes), distribution shift, and mitigation of propagated teacher errors or biases. Practitioners should treat KD as a flexible framework that must be adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers capabilities of large models into smaller ones via indirect supervision. Methods vary by what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single, ensemble, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and practical constraints (limited data, privacy, cross-distribution generalization, modality mismatch). Empirical work across speech, vision, language, retrieval, graph, generative modeling, and medical imaging shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while gaining resource efficiency; theoretical analyses and diagnostic studies clarify mechanisms and guide designs such as projector layers, many-to-many layer mapping, and curriculum or data-augmentation strategies. Remaining challenges include distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, robust transfer of inductive biases, and principled layer-to-layer alignment for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Yet Contextual, Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has repeatedly enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost across modalities while retaining much of the performance of larger models. Empirical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, inductive biases, and task-specific capabilities from teacher to student, and can be adapted via logit-, feature-, and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, adversarial procedures, and data- or privacy-aware variants. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization difficulties, teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity, and propagation of teacher errors limit its effectiveness unless combined with careful protocol design and complementary compression techniques. I argue KD should be treated as a first-class tool in compression toolkits, but only when used with task-aware filtering, capacity-aware targets, and architecture- or data-aware refinements to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical, widely used toolbox to transfer behavior and representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, resource-efficient students. The approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel statistics, or generated samples), whether original training data are available, and whether the objective emphasizes efficiency, privacy, robustness, or interpretability. Across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, carefully designed distillation objectives and training pipelines—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—produce compact models that approach teacher performance under deployment constraints. Key practical challenges are capacity and optimization mismatch between teacher and student, data- and privacy-limited settings, distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher traits; promising responses include task-aware filtering of teacher signals, multi-layer mapping strategies, data-free sample synthesis, and privacy-preserving noise mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Principled Toolbox for Practical and Responsible Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolbox that can produce compact, deployable models when combined with complementary design choices. Properly applied—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to map layers, and which auxiliary techniques to use (pretraining, curriculum, adversarial or privacy safeguards)—KD can deliver students that approach or sometimes match teacher performance while enabling latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployment. At the same time, KD has clear failure modes (data heterogeneity, low-frequency phenomena, imperfect teachers, and optimization challenges) that demand targeted mitigations rather than blind application.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-label supervision to representation and feature matching—and has been adapted for online, multi-teacher, self-supervised, data-free, cross-modal, and federated scenarios. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections determines the success of compression. Best results arise when distillation is combined with complementary techniques (architecture adaptation, quantization, pruning, or curriculum strategies) and when practitioners attend to data-availability, distribution shift, and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Path for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from teacher models. Across tasks and modalities, distillation methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and structure-preserving objectives—enable deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory use, and communication cost. Distillation also serves as a flexible substrate for addressing domain adaptation, lifelong learning, robustness, low-precision deployment, and generator compression. However, realizing these benefits in practice requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to map layers and representations, how to handle limited or private teacher data, and how to mitigate bias or robustness loss.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. KD methods vary by what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structure), how teachers and students are paired (single, ensemble, multi-teacher, or self-distillation), and by constraints on data, privacy, and deployment hardware. Across vision, language, speech, graphs, and reinforcement learning, KD produces compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while enabling lower latency, lower memory, and operation under communication- or privacy-constrained settings. However, gains depend on teacher quality, data used for distillation, and architectural alignment; practical pipelines therefore combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design choices to close optimization and generalization gaps.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Demand-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' utility. KD methods span output matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, self- and ensemble-distillation, meta-learned and student-friendly teacher designs, and data- or task-aware adaptations. Empirical work across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks demonstrates KD’s ability to deliver large reductions in model size and compute with modest performance loss, and in many cases to improve robustness or generalization when combined with appropriate procedures. At the same time, KD’s reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these constraints through architectural design, curriculum and meta-learning, augmentation and synthetic-data strategies, and multi-teacher or online schemes is central to practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.
